interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body:
The prognosis is driven by several significant factors, including a preoperative PSA of 16.8 and an ISUP grade group 5 Gleason pattern on the prostatectomy specimen. Further adverse findings include pathological T4 stage, positive surgical margins, seminal vesicle invasion, and lymphovascular invasion. These elements suggest advanced local disease burden.

Countervailing or mitigating information is limited; specifically, there was no documented lymph node metastasis in the surgical report. The biopsy-to-prostatectomy comparison is not possible as the pathology report notes only one biopsy session with missing Gleason pattern/ISUP data. Missing postoperative PSA and follow-up trajectory significantly widen prognostic uncertainty regarding recurrence risk assessment. Information regarding subsequent PSA levels and their trend would be crucial for refining this prognosis. The fixed estimated horizon is 34.46 months. This is a predicted recurrence horizon, not evidence of observed recurrence. The sensitivity range is 25.85–43.08 months; its coverage has not been validated.
